model_annotation: The plot illustrates the coverage achieved by four different language model configurations—Llama-3B, Llama-3B + FT, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT—as a function of the number of completions (k), which is displayed on the x-axis on a logarithmic scale ranging from 2⁰ to 2⁸ (i.e., 1 to 256). The y-axis represents coverage, scaled linearly from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks at 0.2 intervals. Each model is represented by a distinct line with a unique color and marker: Llama-3B is shown as a solid blue line with circular markers, Llama-3B + FT as a solid dark green line with triangular markers, Llama-1B as a solid light blue line with circular markers, and Llama-1B + FT as a solid light green line with triangular markers. All four lines show a generally increasing trend in coverage as k increases, starting from approximately 0.4 (Llama-3B and Llama-3B + FT) and 0.2 (Llama-1B and Llama-1B + FT) at k = 2⁰, and rising to approximately 0.85–0.9 at k = 2⁸. The Llama-3B and Llama-3B + FT lines are consistently above the Llama-1B and Llama-1B + FT lines across all k values, with the Llama-3B + FT line slightly outperforming Llama-3B and Llama-1B + FT slightly outperforming Llama-1B. The lines are smooth and exhibit no sharp changes or plateaus, indicating a steady increase in coverage with more completions.
